q: Does RPE retain Heisenberg scaling for two-qubit entangling gate calibration (e.g., CNOT / CZ / cross-resonance) with realistic crosstalk, and how does the ladder generation strategy generalize when the gate has multiple independent systematic error parameters (ZZ over-rotation, single-qubit phase leakage, control-target asymmetry)?
basis: KLY sec. IV.C sketches nested single-qubit RPE for a universal gate set but does not directly address two-qubit gates; subsequent RPE-for-2Q work (Rudinger et al. 2017, Meier et al. 2019) exists but was not replicated here, and the paper's abstract restricts to 'universal single-qubit gate-set'.
next_steps: Extend rpe_sim.py to a 2-qubit statevector simulator with parameterized CR(theta) + IX/IZ/ZI/ZZ residuals; define cos/sin analogues using two-qubit Pauli measurements (e.g. XI, YI in a Bell basis); repeat the K=1..14 sweep and fit sigma vs N; compare against the tightened Rudinger 2017 constants.

q: How does RPE precision degrade under time-varying (non-stationary) noise where the gate's over-rotation epsilon drifts on the same timescale as the ladder acquisition (e.g., slow 1/f flux noise on superconducting qubits)?
basis: KLY assumes a fixed unknown phase A during the estimation; Heisenberg scaling proof implicitly requires stationarity across the K generations. The paper does not model drift, and this is the dominant failure mode in real calibration workflows (drift beats the ladder faster than shot noise).
next_steps: Modify rpe_sim.py to inject a stochastic epsilon(t) with configurable OU-process or 1/f PSD; sweep the drift correlation time tau_drift against the total wall-clock time of the ladder T_ladder; identify the tau_drift/T_ladder ratio below which RPE loses its N^-1 advantage vs a shot-noise-only estimator; propose an interleaved-generation schedule that hedges against drift.

q: Can a hybrid RPE+RB protocol combine RPE's sample efficiency for systematic parameters with RB's robustness to arbitrary stochastic noise, and what is the sample-complexity Pareto frontier?
basis: KLY sec. VI positions RPE as an alternative to randomized benchmarking (RB) for systematic-error calibration; RB (Magesan et al. 2011) instead reports an average error rate that folds systematic + stochastic together. No side-by-side head-to-head sample-complexity study was run in this replication.
next_steps: Add code/rb_baseline.py implementing standard Clifford RB on the same R_x(pi/2+epsilon) circuit; measure the sample count needed for RB to detect the same epsilon at 3-sigma vs the RPE run at each K; plot RPE vs RB on a common (samples, detected precision) axis; then prototype a hybrid where RB gates the stochastic error budget and RPE reads out the residual coherent phase.

q: How sensitive is the RPE estimator to the specific hardware noise model (T1 relaxation, dephasing T2, readout confusion matrix, leakage to |2>) and does the paper's SPAM-robustness proof (Sec. IV) survive realistic superconducting/trapped-ion device parameters?
basis: KLY sec. IV proves robustness to a specific SPAM-error model with additive constants delta_prep, delta_meas; the paper does not simulate T1/T2/leakage/readout-confusion. Our replication ran a noiseless simulator (Sec 4.1 REPORT.md, listed as C4=Not tested), so the robustness claim is confirmed only theoretically here.
next_steps: Re-run the sweep against Qiskit FakeManila / FakeGuadalupe (real IBMQ calibration snapshots including readout confusion matrix); separately parametrize T1 in [50us, 200us] and T2 in [30us, 150us]; identify the (T1,T2) region where the RPE slope stays within 10% of -1.0 vs where it degrades to -0.5 (shot-noise plateau); compare against KLY's analytic delta_prep/delta_meas bound.

q: Can a machine-learning (e.g., transformer / RNN) decoder trained on RPE bitstream patterns extract phase estimates with lower variance than the atan2 estimator (Eq. V.3), particularly in the low-M / low-shot regime where the atan2 discretization noise dominates?
basis: KLY uses a fixed atan2-of-empirical-frequencies estimator which is asymptotically optimal but not necessarily finite-shot optimal (recent Bayesian-MLE-for-phase-estimation work, e.g. Wiebe & Granade 2016 on Bayesian PE, suggests substantial gains at small M). No ML-decoder experiments were run here.
next_steps: Generate a labeled training corpus by running rpe_sim.py with known true A across a dense grid; train (a) a Bayesian MLE estimator and (b) a small transformer taking the (n0_j, n+_j, k_j) sequence as input and outputting A-hat; compare RMSE-vs-N vs the atan2 baseline; check whether the decoder respects Heisenberg scaling asymptotically while beating atan2 finite-shot.
